rules: A controller-process death MUST NOT be reported as a worker-process death.
A static/source audit MUST NOT be promoted to executed mutant evidence.
BLOCKED and INCONCLUSIVE remain benchmark-ineligible for every critical mutant.
Semantic operation identity must remain stable across retry/restart unless T16 intentionally mutates configuration or identity inputs.
Stale authority must be measured by attempting a late completion after a newer owner/attempt exists, not inferred from documentation alone.
Every execution must record the actual process/container killed and the durable authority that remained alive.

T5.primitive: two competing Worker processes on the same task queue plus one semantic objective
T5.acceptance: only current task authority may commit; stale completion must not become authoritative

T7.primitive: SIGKILL Worker after oracle apply and before Activity result is durably acknowledged
T7.acceptance: recovery is observable; duplicate external apply is prevented by stable operation identity/provider policy or reported as ambiguous, never silently successful

T8.primitive: oracle applies once then loses response
T8.acceptance: same operation identity is reused and total external applyCount remains 1

T11.primitive: race workflow cancellation against Worker crash/restart
T11.acceptance: post-cancel unauthorized progress cannot become terminal success

T12.primitive: hold old Activity completion until a newer attempt/owner exists, then submit stale completion
T12.acceptance: stale completion is rejected or cannot overwrite current authority

T16.primitive: restart same workflow with intentionally changed runtime/tool/config identity under controlled variants
T16.acceptance: semantic incompatibility is rejected, surfaced as nondeterminism/configuration incompatibility, or explicitly migrated; never silently changes recovery meaning

T5.primitive: two executors contend for the same workflow identity with explicit executor identities
T5.acceptance: only valid owner may advance/commit terminal state; stale executor cannot overwrite terminal result

T7.primitive: SIGKILL executor after oracle apply and before step/workflow result persistence
T7.acceptance: recovery preserves operation identity; duplicate external apply is prevented by provider policy or ambiguity is surfaced

T8.primitive: oracle applies once then loses response
T8.acceptance: retry/recovery uses same operation identity and applyCount remains 1

T11.primitive: race cancellation/stop authority against executor crash and pending-workflow recovery
T11.acceptance: cancelled authority cannot later be overwritten by recovered stale work

T12.primitive: delay completion from old executor until a newer executor/owner exists
T12.acceptance: old executor cannot overwrite newer or terminal state

T16.primitive: recover workflow under changed applicationVersion/executor/tool configuration variants
T16.acceptance: incompatible recovery must fail closed or be explicitly versioned/migrated; wrong-workflow semantics are forbidden

candidates.workerKillTarget: service endpoint process hosting Restate handler

T5.primitive: concurrent endpoint attempts/ownership transition for same workflow invocation
T5.acceptance: fencing prevents stale attempt effects from becoming authoritative

T7.primitive: SIGKILL endpoint after oracle apply and before ctx.run result persistence
T7.acceptance: documented duplicate window is measured; stable operation identity/provider policy prevents second apply or ambiguity remains explicit

T8.primitive: oracle applies once then loses response inside ctx.run
T8.acceptance: re-execution preserves operation identity and applyCount remains 1 under provider idempotency policy

T11.primitive: race invocation cancellation against endpoint SIGKILL/restart
T11.acceptance: cancelled invocation cannot later become successful through stale progress

T12.primitive: delay old-attempt completion until invocation fencing token changes
T12.acceptance: old token/attempt cannot overwrite current invocation authority

T16.primitive: restart endpoint with changed handler/tool/config/version variants while retaining invocation identity
T16.acceptance: semantic incompatibility is explicit; journal replay must not silently execute a different meaning

candidates.workerKillTarget: self-hosted worker/task process or container; controller adapter is explicitly not a valid T7 kill target

T5.primitive: force competing worker/run-attempt authority for one run and retain stale snapshot completion
T5.acceptance: stale snapshot/worker cannot complete or overwrite current run authority

T7.primitive: SIGKILL actual worker/task process after oracle apply before run completion checkpoint
T7.acceptance: actual CRASHED semantics and external-effect duplication behavior are measured; controller death is not accepted as substitute

T8.primitive: oracle applies once then loses response from task attempt
T8.acceptance: same operation identity is reused across any task retry and applyCount remains 1

T11.primitive: race runs.cancel against actual worker crash/retry/restart
T11.acceptance: cancelled run cannot later complete successfully through stale worker progress

T12.primitive: retain stale snapshot/attempt completion until newer snapshot authority exists
T12.acceptance: stale completion is rejected and cannot overwrite current snapshot/run state

T16.primitive: resume/replay same objective under changed deployment/task/config identity variants
T16.acceptance: version/config mismatch is explicit and cannot silently reinterpret prior durable work
